lines:
Responsibilities: Owns Chat-scoped job identity and lifecycle for every asynchronous capability producer. A job's runner is either a supervised OS process session (shell, shell_start, python, python_start) or a delegated background child Agent run (tool.subagent, tool.subagent_fork, tool.subagent_message); the kind is registry data, not a second scheduler. It owns durable start intents and observations, running and terminal snapshots, bounded output cursors and window or tail reads, collection acknowledgement, explicit release, retained-work disposition, capacity, keep/stop/input/list/release control routing, and the completion gate a final assistant answer must pass.

Owned state: one JobRecord per job with kind (process or subagent), owner Chat, invoking Agent/child scope, model-facing label, running/terminal snapshot, captured-output byte counts and cursor, collected/kept/released/interrupted disposition, the byte counts recorded at discard, and - for a child job - the delegated child identity and its terminal outcome. Child live progress (one line per model turn) and the child's own job inventory are registry facts; the child's conversation and evidence remain the child scope's and are never merged into the parent transcript.

Contracts: the durable broker authorizes each control (job_output, job_input, job_stop, job_keep, job_list, job_release) and the registry settles it. job_output returns status, bounded cursor output, the captured stdout/stderr byte totals and the remaining byte count, and - in tail mode - the last window of each stream with the omitted byte count; for a child job it returns kind=subagent with its durable childId, live progress and terminal outcome. job_input steers a running child at its next step boundary or resumes a settled child as a new background turn-set, and sends stdin to a process. job_stop cancels the runner and closes a child scope so it can never be resumed. job_keep records deliberate retention so the delegating Agent may finish while the work continues; asked about a finished or detached job it answers with kept=false and the resolution path instead of a failure. job_release records that the Agent is done with a finished job without reading it, optionally discarding its captured logs while keeping status, exit code and byte counts, and refuses a running job with a pointer to stop or keep. completion_notice_scoped reports a bounded summary of unresolved jobs to the Agent loop - running and unretained, or terminal and neither collected nor released: a byte budget, an explicit omitted count, job_list as the way to enumerate the rest, and job_release as the cheap exit. The notice can never grow with the number of jobs, and the delegating Agent's notice is scoped exactly as its controls are.

Invariants: jobs never cross Chat boundaries, and a control is additionally scoped to the exact delegating Agent/child where one applies. Identity is committed before the side effect, and a terminal state is committed before it can be observed as collected or released. Process runners retain complete descendant-tree control; child runners use the child's own cancellation token and stop the child-scoped jobs they still own. Capacity bounds live and retained jobs (8 per Chat, 32 total) and a refused start is an explicit typed failure rather than a silent drop. A terminal job the model has not resolved is not evictable, so the notice summarizes rather than enumerates; a released job is evictable like a collected one. A job a delegated child starts must be collectable by that child - its record scope and the child's control scope agree - or the child reports it to the delegating Agent explicitly instead of leaving it uncollected under the parent.

Failure and recovery: restart marks every running job interrupted, releases retention, and never replays it; a process tree cannot be reconstructed from a PID and a child is not re-run. A child job's committed frame is then reported interrupted rather than running, and a continuation starts a fresh turn-set from the child's committed head. Collection is acknowledged only after the broker durably records the returned output, so a crash before that boundary leaves it readable again; a release is durable once recorded, and a failed save leaves the job unresolved rather than silently resolved.

Performance and NFRs: one supervisor pass drives runner snapshots and persistence; output is read by cursor or as a bounded tail from captured logs instead of buffered in memory; a kind index serves control lookups; bounded job history is evicted oldest-first only when terminal and resolved (collected or released); no job control requires a project.

Non-responsibilities: no capability authorization or approval decision (Invocation Broker), no OS process spawning, health or descendant-tree mechanics (Process-Tree Supervisor), no graph scheduling or Agent-loop execution (Workflow Runtime Worker), no canonical semantic history, and no secret materialization.

data.name: Chat Job Registry & Completion Barrier
data.technology: Rust owner-scoped job registry over supervised process and delegated-child runners
